name: slow
title: SLOW — timelocked transfers with a reverse
description: The SLOW dapp as one self-contained HTML document, served from contract bytecode over ERC-8244, ERC-5219 and ERC-4804.
pageNote: `page` is what is pinned, chunked and deployed; `pageSource` is what is read and tested. They differ by comments and indentation only - 82,651 bytes of them, four chunks, about 30% of the deployment. scripts/minify.mjs builds one from the other and test/minify.test.mjs holds them together; scripts/test.sh runs the whole page suite against BOTH.

deployed.note: Live on all three chains at one address each, verified by scripts/validate-bridge.mjs (29/29). Stewardship was set in SlowPage's constructor, never transferred, so the deployer held nothing at any point. Chunk addresses differ per chain because they are plain CREATE; the four CREATE3 addresses do not.

verification.etherscan: All six on chains 1 and 8453. Robinhood Chain's explorer is a Blockscout instance behind a challenge that refuses automated submission.
verification.sourcify: 17 of 18. Every contract is an exact_match on all three chains except SlowArrival on 4663, where Sourcify reports bytecode_length_mismatch against the creation bytecode. Its RUNTIME is byte-identical across all three (4,916 B, checked on chain), and the same source is an exact_match on 1 and 8453, so the code is the same code — it is the attestation that is missing on that one chain, not the match.
verification.checksumNote: SlowLens was first recorded here with a wrong EIP-55 checksum, which Sourcify rejected as an invalid address. The correct form is 0xC9c4a3d3Dd3714B08b2138080F1D143585531d4D.

deployed.gateNote: SLOWGate is not deployed by hand: SLOW's constructor CREATE2s it at a fixed salt, so it lands at the same address wherever SLOW does. It custodies relayer tips, which is why it is listed here and verified — deploying by address alone had missed it. Its runtime is 1,808 bytes on all three chains; `forge build --sizes` reports 1,805 for the standalone artifact, because the deployed one is created inline by SLOW's constructor. The chain is the number a watcher should pin. Its runtime is 1,808 bytes on all three chains, three more than `forge build --sizes` reports for the standalone artifact; the pinned number is the one the chain actually holds, since the point of pinning it is to notice a change.

orphans.note: Deployed by mistake and referenced by nothing. Left recorded so nobody mistakes them for part of the deployment.
orphans.reason: A salt nonce passed as decimal 1359136113 instead of 1359456113 (0x5107a771), which put the first bridge pair on Ethereum at unpublished addresses. Redeployed at the correct salt; these two are inert.

protocol.note: This is the canonical SLOW: one build at one address on every chain listed. Source is src/SLOW.sol. src/SLOWv1.sol is the frozen source of an earlier, separate deployment that shares no state with this one and is not referenced by this page.

deployment.sourceNote: This address is SlowPage, not SLOW. It read src/SLOW.sol and that was wrong in the one file that governs an irreversible deployment: chunks.artifact names SlowPage, test/deploy.rehearsal.mjs deploys out/SlowPage.sol/SlowPage.json here with this salt and asserts it lands, and the constructor encoding it builds matches SlowPage(address,address,address,address[],bytes32) argument for argument. The protocol contract is a separate deployment with its own salt; see protocol.

verified.permissioned: Salt bytes[0:20] are the steward, so only that address reaches this contract address. A different sender deploying the same salt lands elsewhere (checked: 0x8179a1CE...).
verified.chainIndependent: Salt byte[20] is CreateX's redeploy-protection flag and MUST stay 0x00. Setting it mixes block.chainid into the guarded salt and yields three different addresses.
verified.method: Simulated CreateX.deployCreate3 as the steward on all three chains; identical result. scripts/address.mjs reproduces it offline via createxAddress().

bridge.note: SlowArrival and SlowRelay, CREATE3 through the same steward and deployer as the page. Addresses derived before deployment and checked free on all three chains.

constructorArgs: message deliverers: both on chain 1, none on an L2

verified.method: test/DeployBridgeFork.t.sol runs the live CreateX on forks of 1, 8453 and 4663 with DIFFERENT constructor arguments on each and asserts one address. scripts/address.mjs reproduces the derivation offline.
verified.whyItMatters: SlowRelay.receiveRelay accepts a proof only when the recovered origin equals address(this). Diverging addresses would stop settlement silently.

proven.note: Legs demonstrated on mainnet, not only on forks. Each entry is a real transaction whose effect was read back from chain state afterwards.

ethereum-to-robinhood.branch: SlowOrigin.recover branch 4 — Nitro aliases every retryable sender including EOAs, so the origin comes from the checked hint
ethereum-to-robinhood.verified: SLOW.pendingTransfers[tid].from == SlowArrival, SlowArrival.originOf[tid] == the L1 sender

ethereum-to-base.branch: SlowOrigin.recover branch 5 — OP Stack aliases only contract senders, so an EOA arrives unaliased and is its own origin (authenticated=false)
ethereum-to-base.verified: originOf[tid] == the L1 sender; that sender then called SlowArrival.reverse and the ETH returned (balance +19372758702892 wei, the amount less gas). originOf cleared, SlowArrival ETH balance back to 0. This is the round trip the contract exists for, end to end on mainnet.

unproven: L2 -> L1 OP finalisation (SlowArrival.forward): needs the ~7 day withdrawal window
L2 -> L1 ArbSys exit on Orbit (SlowRelay.proveFill): needs the ~6.4 day challenge period
SlowRelay end to end: needs a funded relayer with inventory on both legs

pending.note: Both initiated 2026-09-06 with dust and bounty zero (operating rule 1). Each exercises a SlowOrigin.recover branch no live transaction has taken yet. Neither can be hurried; both need a second L1 transaction once their window opens.

base-to-ethereum.branch: branch 1 — msg.sender is the OptimismPortal, so l2Sender() answers and the origin is AUTHENTICATED
base-to-ethereum.remaining: prove once the output root posts (~1-2h), then finalise after the 7 day challenge period
base-to-ethereum.hazard: finalizeWithdrawalTransaction marks the withdrawal finalized BEFORE calling the target and does not revert on failure, so a revert in arrive would strand the ETH permanently. Bounty is zero, which is what keeps the EIP-7702 finaliser defect out of reach.

robinhood-to-ethereum.branch: branch 3 — msg.sender is the BRIDGE, so activeOutbox() then l2ToL1Sender() answers; also AUTHENTICATED
robinhood-to-ethereum.remaining: execute through the Outbox with a merkle proof after the ~6.4 day challenge period
robinhood-to-ethereum.note: Arbitrum reverts atomically on a failed execution, so unlike the OP leg this message stays replayable.

relay-open.leg: SlowRelay.open on Base — the first live use of the relay contract
relay-open.verified: statusOf reads OPEN; the id in the Opened event equals the one derived from the fields independently. relayer/index.mjs found it on chain, recomputed the id, read the escrow from the source and the fill state from the destination, priced it at ~57% apr over the 6.4 day return leg and reported WOULD FILL.
relay-open.escrowUnlocks: fillDeadline + PROOF_GRACE (8 days) — cancellable from 2026-09-14, recovering the dust

relay-fill.leg: SlowRelay fill + proveFill, Base -> Robinhood, by a live relayer
relay-fill.verified: filledBy[id] on Robinhood is the relayer; the recipient holds the delivered SLOW position; the relayer paid it out of its own inventory. Source still reads OPEN with provenBy zero, which is correct — the proof travels by ArbSys and needs the ~6.4 day challenge period before release can be called.
relay-fill.remaining: release on Base once provenBy is set, ~6.4 days from 2026-09-06
relay-fill.note: The relayer is scripts/relayer.mjs for the decision and relayer/index.mjs for the loop, running as a Render background worker. It found the intent unaided, recomputed the id, and fronted the destination leg.
